PRIVACY & PHI RESPONSIBILITIES

Privacy & Facility Data Responsibilities

Updated: October 4, 2026 · Deployment guidance; not an executed privacy agreement or BAA

Patient Health Information Safeguards

Hosting safeguards

Verify TLS, database encryption, backup encryption, and key custody in the selected deployment.

Decision audit records

Protected decisions record the authenticated actor. Retention and tamper resistance require deployment validation.

Resident data boundaries

Do not send resident records to public demos, SDK labs, advertising services, or unapproved AI providers.

01.Scope & Deployment Review

This page describes current product boundaries and responsibilities for facilities considering ShorelineOps. It does not establish a legal entity, execute a Business Associate Agreement (BAA), or certify HIPAA compliance.

Before processing resident information, identify the contracting parties, permitted uses, hosting providers, and applicable agreements with the facility and qualified privacy counsel.

02.Resident Information Boundaries

Resident records support dietary operations, clinical review, and tray verification. Use only information necessary for approved workflows and limit access to authorized staff.

Public demos use synthetic information. The isolated Muse SDK laboratory has no resident-record or database connection. Any future AI or device integration requires a separately reviewed data boundary before facility use.

03.Technical Safeguards & Architecture

Clinical operations require one facility per deployment and database. Shared multi-facility clinical isolation is not established.

  • Server-side permissions restrict protected actions, including clinical reconciliation and purchasing approval.
  • Authentication uses bcrypt password hashing and signed access tokens. Configure session expiry and available multi-factor authentication for shared devices.
  • Validate HTTPS, encryption at rest, backup security, access policies, audit retention, and incident response in the actual deployment.

These controls support privacy procedures; source inspection alone does not prove regulatory compliance.

04.Agreements Required Before Rollout

A facility handling PHI must establish applicable business associate and subcontractor agreements before rollout. Executed agreements should define permitted processing, incident reporting, access requests, retention, termination, and secure disposal responsibilities.

No breach-notification deadline or data-destruction guarantee is created by this informational page.

05.Facility BAA Review

Confirm the availability and terms of a facility-specific BAA with the contracting parties before entering PHI. Automated BAA onboarding and a downloadable signed agreement are not currently represented as available product features.

Review security and deployment responsibilities alongside your hosting arrangements and facility procedures.

06.Reporting & Facility Contacts

Use the security reporting instructions in the project security policy for suspected vulnerabilities. Do not include resident records or credentials in public issues.

Facility privacy requests and legal notices must use contacts established in the applicable executed service agreement.
